text:
mike: Quick Q — after merging TF PR that adds an initContainer to read a projected sa token, a few backend pods intermittently fail on start. The flow was: apply creates aws_iam_role, then a separate apply patches the k8s ServiceAccount with eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn. Some pods (created in same CI run) crash with init errors saying token file missing. Anyone seen a race between SA annotation + pod creation?

sasha: Yep, seen this before. K8s doesn't magically re-inject projected tokens for already-running pods when you patch the SA. If the Deployment gets created before the SA has the annotation, pods may not have the expected projected token mount. Short fixes: force a rolling restart after the SA patch, or ensure the SA + annotation exist before creating the Deployment. :thumbsup:

mike: Got it — logs from the initContainer look like this:
```
Error: open /var/run/secrets/tokens/aws-token: no such file or directory
init: exiting
```

julia: Two practical approaches:
1) Terraform ordering: create the kubernetes_service_account with the annotation in the same plan as the deployment so the SA exists annotated when the deployment is created. If you need separate aws_iam_role creation, make sure the role exists and then annotate the SA referencing the role arn *before* the Deployment resource. Use explicit depends_on on the Deployment to wait for the SA resource.
2) Make the initContainer resilient: loop/wait for the token file for a short timeout (10-30s) so transient ordering gaps don't fail the pod.

sasha: Example TF snippet we used to enforce ordering (simplified):
```
resource "aws_iam_role" "app_role" { ... }
resource "kubernetes_service_account" "app_sa" {
  metadata {
    name = "app-sa"
    namespace = kubernetes_namespace.app.metadata[0].name
    annotations = {
      "eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn" = aws_iam_role.app_role.arn
    }
  }
}
resource "kubernetes_deployment" "app" {
  # ensure deployment waits for SA
  depends_on = [kubernetes_service_account.app_sa]
  ...
}
```

ben: Another gotcha — if you annotate an existing SA after pods were created, the projected token volume may still appear but the token audience/claims might not match the role trust condition until token rotation happens (token TTL). So restart is often easiest. Also confirm your IAM role trust policy uses the correct namespace/name (sub) and OIDC provider.

mike: We deploy via CI that runs `terraform apply` then kubectl apply for k8s manifests. Sounds like we should switch to creating the SA (annotated) via Terraform and make the k8s manifest apply depend on TF completion. Would also add a short wait/retry in the initContainer for robustness.

infra-bot: CI: terraform apply (plan id: plan-8473) succeeded for staging. Deployment job enqueued (job id: deploy-992).

julia: If you want to be extra safe, annotate the SA in TF and then `kubectl rollout restart` the Deployment as part of the pipeline step after TF apply. That covers old pods and any token TTL edge-cases.

mike: Thanks, will update the PR to move SA creation/annotation into TF and add depends_on on the deployment + initContainer backoff. Will ping when it's updated.
